idea.title: Grow rammers: a short dragon that sees a 10+ enemy head holds its ordinary split until it is long enough to sprint-ram from 4-5 steps (P.rammerLength)
idea.hypothesis: Complement of I323 (MISSES 21: reach needs length). A k-step sprint costs k-1 segments and needs length 3+ before each extra step, so a ram from 4-5 steps needs a dragon 5-6 long. The leaders' long rams come from such dragons: rank 1 in 291888 made 9 rams on 10+ heads from 3-4 steps, each by a dragon 3 long at impact (5-6 before the sprint), e.g. r350 dragon 559, 4 long, sprinted N,E (eating a pearl),N,N into a 30-long head; rank 2 (801) in 291895 started 54 rams on 10+ heads, 34 of them from 4-7 steps. The champion's started head-ons in this review's 8 kept rule games: 331, the rammer 2-3 long at impact in 297 (90%), none from 4+ steps (P.maxRamSteps 3), and its dragons split at P.splitAtLength 4, so few are ever 5+ before the fold (E0121's coder: a 5+-long rammer fires on about one map in twelve). So I323's reach of min(6, length-1) has few dragons to use it. Change, behind P.growRammers with P.rammerLength (start 6), P.rammerPreyLength (start 10) and P.rammerMemory (start 10 rounds): before P.foldRound, a dragon shorter than P.rammerLength that has seen an enemy head of visibleLen >= P.rammerPreyLength in the last P.rammerMemory rounds skips its ordinary split (shouldSplit's ordinary path only; split-outs, sheds and the cap rules unchanged). Measure first with a logging copy on 8 maps (4 of 2400+ tiles) against champion and breeder: turns a game on which a dragon 4-5 long sees a 10+ enemy head before r397 (stop with the numbers if under 5 a game), splits held, and rams of 4+ steps landed and their victims' lengths. Scenarios, lengths through P: a 4-long dragon at r150 with a 14-long enemy head 5 steps away doesn't split at P.splitAtLength, and at P.rammerLength rams it from 4 steps along a clear path; boundary: with the prey P.rammerPreyLength - 1 long it splits as today; from P.foldRound nothing changes. Default bounds, map mix big 0.5 (10+ enemy heads before the fold are common locally only on big maps).

session.name: bc-E0182-3bc2dd4f
session.summary:
I didn't commit anything for I351: the idea's own stop line fired. The clone is back at 02cebbd with a clean tree.

**What I measured.** I built a shadow copy that plays exactly like the champion but logs where the new hold would act, plus a logging copy of the candidate. They played the champion and the breeder on 8 fresh maps (4 big maps of 2400+ tiles, 4 eval maps), both sides: 64 games, 32 of them shadow games.
- **Stop line (under 5 a game):** a dragon 4-5 long sees a 10+ enemy head before r397 on 0.69 turns a game (95% 0.09–1.28, n = 32 games). The whole interval is below 5, so the line fires.
- **Splits held:** the hold would have changed 1 split in 32 shadow games (chance range 0.006–0.157 a game). Against the champion, the candidate's games were identical to the champion's (0 splits held).
- **Why it barely fires:** 86 of the 90 such turns in the shadow games, and 106 of 112 in the logging games' count, came with our team already at 62+ dragons. At that point ordinary splits are off anyway, because of the 64-dragon cap less the rescue reserve. Locally, 10+ enemy heads show up only on big maps and only once our team is full, and there dragons already grow past 4. The idea assumes a dragon that sees such a head would otherwise split at 4, and that isn't what happens.
- **Long rams already happen:** in the 16 shadow-vs-champion games there were 21 rams from 4+ steps (1.3  [...] agons before the cap. The `midking` screen entry is the only local opponent that does that on smaller maps; it isn't in the rotation, and I didn't test against it.

Messages to the orchestrator: the start notice and the final no-code summary both sent successfully.

Choices: none built (measure-first stop); scope measured = dragons 4-5 long before r397 seeing an enemy head with visibleLen ≥ 10 in the last 10 rounds.

Blocked by: at the 64 cap ordinary splits are already off, so the hold has nothing to change on big maps; no rotation opponent grows 10+ dragons before we reach the cap.

idea.title: Dead-end farms must beat the dragon's own intake: enter a closed pocket only when its net pearls per round of the trip beat what this dragon eats a round outside, and a folder's trip must fit its fold budget
idea.hypothesis: Farm audit of bot/farm.hpp with measurement. farmEntryOk lets a dragon enter a closed pocket when it counts P.farmMinPearls (2) visible pearls or empty fast tiles inside. At the end, splitOutLength leaves a length-2 parent to die: that is -2 length, and its one dropped pearl lies at the dead end, where the child (our reversed rear) walks away from it. So a farm trip gains net length only above 2 pearls. A throwaway output_log copy of champion 351cbcd (unswbc-1.0.0; 76 games against itself and the gauntlet 'swarm', 9 ladder plus 10 eval-style maps, seeds 77100-77109) paired each farm entry (closed best move accepted by farmEntryOk) with that dragon's next forced split-out. Mean length gained before the split-out: g0 2.2 (63 episodes), g3 2.3 (37), trauma 2.9 (236), g8 3.5 (43), stronghold 4.5 (43), schooltime 4.6 (27). Episodes gaining <= 2 (net zero or a loss, plus the rounds spent, a mean of 3-14): 78%, 78%, 50%, 53%, 2% and 56%. I224 (farmMinPearls 3) is merged here. Fold window (I476, merged here; champion 02cebbd rule counts, 24 games, 8 kept replays): 397 of the 685 farm-entry turns (58%) fell in r397-498, and 91% of those were followed by a split-out within 30 rounds. In the 8 kept replays (losses first, so suggestive), fold-window trips that ended in a split-out: our longest dragon's 10 trips ate 3.6 pearls in 5.0 rounds, net +1.6 after the parent (0.32 a round) against its 0.376 pearls a round over all 824 longest-dragon rounds of r397-499; the other dragons' 72 trips (mean length 17) ate 2.54 in 4.5 rounds, net +0.54 (0.12 a round), and 13 more never split out within 30 rounds; pre-fold farm-entry turns by short dragons ate 2.65 each within their trip (86 turns). A split-out child is born long with its body out of view (dragons born 8+ log body < len on 21% of 22,138 turns; born 2, 0.01%) and 18.6% of split-out children split out again within 5 rounds (n 4,791, against 2.3% of ordinary split children), so each trip can start a chain. General quantity (sig 2026-09-27: formulae, not hard cutoffs): net length per round a trip earns against what the same dragon earns a round outside trips; a fixed pearl count (2, or 2 + P.farmMinNet) stood in for it, the same in every phase and for every dragon. Change, behind P.farmOnRate: farmEntryOk also needs (pearls - P.childLength) / tripRounds >= P.farmRateFactor x ownRate, where tripRounds is one plus the fill's step depth to the farthest counted pearl (floodFill already walks the pocket in distance order) and ownRate this dragon's pearls a round over its last P.intakeWindow (20) rounds (own memory of its length, split-offs added back); a dragon younger than the window keeps today's P.farmMinPearls rule. A dragon with an active fold also needs tripRounds within its fold slack (foldPathCap's budget less its path to the king). P.farmRateFactor (start 1): how much a trip's rate must beat outside intake to pay for its re-split chain risk. Empty fast tiles count at the chance they refill before we reach them (the coder measures it in the logging copy and says what it chose). So the king's fold-window trips (0.32 a round against its 0.376) fail, a folder's trip that eats into its fold time fails, and a hungry short dragon's rich pocket passes. CPU: a division on turns farmEntryOk already runs. Measure first (logging copy, at least 24 games over the rule-count sizes, both sides): per trip, the dragon's role (king, folding, other), phase, pearls eaten before the split-out, rounds, and the same dragon's intake per round outside trips. Stop only if trips net more per round than the dragons' outside intake at sign p <= 0.1 over matched dragons (chance.sign_p), in which case the gate would refuse almost nothing; otherwise build. Report the fold-window rows (kings and folders, r397+) apart from the rest so the phase I476 targeted stays attributable. Scenarios (through P): (1) a length-3 dragon eating 0.1 a round beside a closed 6-tile pocket holding 3 visible pearls 5 steps deep: (3 - 2) / 6 is above 0.1, it enters; the same dragon eating 0.3 a round does not. (2) r420, our king eating 0.376 a round beside a pocket holding 3 pearls 5 deep: it doesn't enter. (3) A folder whose fold budget is 2 rounds beside a 4-deep pocket: it doesn't enter. (4) A dragon younger than the window: today's rule. (5) On Trauma's farm columns (known fast tiles), entries whose realised gain was >= 4 still happen. Report per map: farm episodes, mean gain before split-out, the share <= 2, and pearls per game before and after (Trauma, Stronghold, Schooltime, two generated maps). Siblings: I441 (the king from r300 on 1152+ tiles skips split-out farm trips), I390 and I467 (folders' pearl reach), I121 (the pocket's one-walk count, which sharpens this formula's pearls input).

session.summary: I097 measurement stop fired; no bot change or commit. Logging-only champion a7ec5a9, frozen unswbc 1.1.0, 24 games: 6 maps both sides versus champion and swarm. Net trip intake (pearls minus P.childLength, divided by rounds including split-out) beat the same dragons outside-trip intake in 210 matched dragons versus 155 worse, 137 tied (n=502, one-sided chance.sign_p=0.002319887); the predeclared p<=0.1 stop is met. 504 completed non-overlapping trips; 56 death/game-end censored trips excluded. Restricting trips to <=30 rounds still gives 203 better,150 worse,p=0.002785. Game-level signs are only suggestive: 10 better/6 worse,n=16 farm-bearing games,p=0.227249; do not infer a general gain from correlated dragon samples. Fold-window rows: kings n=55,17 better/27 worse,p(worse)=0.087086; folders n=24,6 better/13 worse,p(worse)=0.083534; early n=376,179 better/101 worse,p(better)=0.000001828. Shadow formula changed 71 scored steps over 24 games, mean 2.958/game,95% mean interval1.251-4.666,36 early/35 late, so the ideas claim that the stop implies almost no refusals is unsupported. Empty fast tiles due by the projected arrival refilled on all136 reached cases,Wilson95%0.973-1.000; no reached not-yet-due cases.
